frameworks.name: Four-Point Availability Lever Framework
frameworks.definition: Four sequential levers that compound show-up rates: time slot density (seven-day/week availability), slot granularity (15-min vs 60-min increments), temporal proximity (same-day or next-day booking preferred), and forward-dragging (moving appointments earlier when possible).

claims.text: Show-up rate optimization is a higher-leverage improvement than close-rate optimization in most organizations; fixing a 25% show-up rate compounds more revenue than fixing sales closing mechanics.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Seven-day-per-week availability (the total number of actual time slots offered across all days) is the primary throughput lever in appointment-based organizations; Alex Hormozi and data scientists analyzing 4,000 daily appointments across industries tested every variable and ranked availability first.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: High availability removes friction for lead scheduling, allowing customers to choose times that fit their lives rather than forcing them into narrow windows.

numbers.axis: appointments per day observed across industries

claims.text: Fifteen-minute time-slot increments (e.g., 3:05 pm, 3:20 pm) convert higher and produce better show rates than 60-minute increments (e.g., 3:00 pm), despite the underlying sales appointment duration remaining 45-60 minutes.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Specific times (3:05 vs 3:00) signal precision and detail to the customer, increasing the perceived seriousness of the appointment and likelihood of punctual attendance.

claims.text: Dragging appointments forward (moving booked appointments earlier when cancellations or openings occur, e.g., pulling a Thursday 4pm appointment to Monday 4pm) increases show-up rates substantially; same-day and next-day appointments show dramatically higher attendance than appointments booked two to four days in the future.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Proximity reduces decision uncertainty and the likelihood that competing priorities emerge; same-day/next-day removes the delay where customers lose motivation or prioritize other tasks.

claims.text: Gym owners reporting poor close rates often have severely constrained availability (e.g., 'sales appointments 7am-9am Tuesdays and Thursdays only'), which is the binding constraint, not their closing ability; availability expansion produces faster revenue growth than closing technique refinement.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: When availability is restricted, disqualified leads (those who cannot make the narrow window) are blamed as 'not serious' when the issue is operational constraint, not buyer intent.
bounded_by: Does not apply to organizations with already-high availability
Does not apply to service models without scheduling constraints

examples.text: Layla wanted to get eyebrow services done in LA. She called the first salon and they had an opening a week out; she declined. She called a second salon offering a four-hour window; she declined. She called a third and they could see her immediately; she went there. The convenience of same-day or immediate availability was the deciding factor, not price, quality, or brand reputation.

A setter-closer team can call a newly-qualified lead and say, 'I see you have an appointment Thursday, but I just had a 4 o'clock cancel today—want me to pull you up to today at 4 o'clock?' The customer accepts the earlier slot. If the team cannot do same-day, they aim for next-day. The pattern repeats across all appointments where possible, prioritizing temporal proximity over the originally-booked date.

practices.text: Offer seven-day-per-week availability for appointment booking, not five-day or weekend-only; ensure every day of the week has time slots open.
Use 15-minute time-slot increments (3:05 pm, 3:20 pm, 3:35 pm) instead of hour increments (3:00 pm, 4:00 pm) to increase show rates and schedule conversion.
Proactively call or message booked leads to offer earlier appointment times whenever cancellations occur; aim for same-day or next-day confirmation rather than multi-day lead time.
When a customer cannot make a proposed time, offer to move them earlier in the calendar (same day or next day) rather than accepting their proposed later date.
